answer: An agent economy resists Sybil by binding actions to identity reputation accrued via peer-attested history. New identities start with zero stake; only continuous correct attestations and jury service raise reputation scores that unlock higher emission shares. Attackers face rising cost: forging a cedar-like durable history across karst-like sparse consensus rounds requires sustained real compute, while any relic of past misbehavior permanently slashes the score and freezes locked balances. Parallel farms collapse under the non-transferable reputation gradient.
